chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him said

The Muhrim (person in Ihram) should not touch anything of the perfume, nor of the basil (or fragrant plant), nor should he delight in it. So whoever is tested by something of that, let him give charity in proportion to what he did, in proportion to his satiety from the food.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (consecration)
key_terms.يَتَلَذَّذُ: To delight or take pleasure in

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a person in Ihram who uses perfume?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar details the prohibition of using perfume or delighting in fragrant plants like basil while in Ihram, emphasizing the purity of the state of consecration. The compensation mechanism, measured by the value of one's satiety, reflects the Shia juristic principle of quantifying spiritual transgressions through tangible economic restitution, a concept rooted in the broader legal framework of Hajj obligations.
